round_1.summary: The core finding reproduces with my own code. Published GT23 moments were not divided by the participant's own mass in most subjects, and the divisor changes between trials of one subject. Exact checks: AB06 normal_walk_1 is the local N·m re-run divided by exactly 71.5 (AB05's README mass); the max residual is 0.0 N·m in all 6 columns, against 17-26 N·m for its own 79.1. AB08 is divided by exactly 62.3 (AB07's), AB05's level walk by 78.9 (AB01's), and AB01 by its own 78.9. The mass-free force-plate estimate agrees: AB06 72.6-73.8, AB08 63.2-63.7, AB05 incline_walk_2 115-120 kg. The re-run files are physical N·m, not published values times a mass, so they are not circular. Returned for wording only: the decision 'why' miscounts, the sheet headline and chip overstate 'another subject's mass' for two subjects that only the force plates estimate, the calibration claim is partly in-sample, and the blinding note omits that the test subjects were known C02 anomalies. The decision is structurally ready; copy it after fix 1. No scientific approval is implied.

checks.name: Is the MotionFile_EH re-run a trustworthy, non-circular reference?
checks.evidence: Provenance: none of the 7038 publisher RawData archive entries contain MotionFile. The files are dated 2024-08-06 to 08-08 (AB05's .sto 2024-10-15), and each ID .sto was written 3-11 min after the IK .mot beside it, subject by subject: a local batch run. The header is the plain OpenSim 'Inverse Dynamics Generalized Forces' with no model or version. AB07's folder is empty, and AB01's ID_results.mot is mislabeled (header IDResults, but it holds coordinates). Not circular: (a) the .sto has finite, physiological right-side moments (AB01 and AB05 right ankle p1 -265 / -278 N·m) where the published right columns are entirely NaN, plus pelvis, lumbar and mtp generalized forces that the published files lack, so it cannot be published values times a mass; (b) against the mass-free lever arm the .sto ankle has slope 0.940-0.986 (8 legs, 5 subjects, corr >= 0.999). If the .sto were 'published x wrong mass' over a correctly normalized publication, those slopes would be 0.71 (AB08), 0.90 (AB06) and 1.10 (AB05). So the .sto is physical N·m, and published = .sto / divisor shows the authors' divisor. Caveats: in AB01 and AB05 the IK file beside the .sto differs from the published angles by up to 0.15 deg, yet the .sto matches published to 0.1 N·m, so the folder's IK and ID are not a consistent pair. AB02, AB03 and AB11 re-runs do not match published by a constant. The right-side .sto moments use plate forces the README calls invalid (broken equipment) and must not be used. Conclusion: usable as an exact reference only where it matches published by a constant (corr 1.0), and validated by force plates, not by provenance.

checks.name: 'Previous subject' pattern vs similar masses
checks.result: pass for the exact cases; overstated for lever-only subjects
checks.evidence: The exact divisors are the one-decimal README / publisher-table values, not model masses: AB06 71.5 gives 0.0 N·m but AB05's model 71.541 gives 0.09-0.14; AB08 62.3 gives 0.0 but 62.261 gives 0.11-0.19. A random divisor would fall within 0.005 kg of one of 12 table values about 0.2 % of the time, so each exact case is a table value, not a near coincidence. Among the exact or near-exact wrong cases (worker's AB09 87.57 and AB13 64.003 are near, with residuals 0.2-0.4 and 3.5-4.7 N·m), 6 of 7 equal the previous subject in README order: AB06, AB08, AB09, AB10, AB12, AB13. AB05's level walk equals AB01 instead. By chance that would be about (1/11)^6, so the pattern is real. Lever-only subjects are not unique under the worker's own ±4.88 % band after bias 0.9942: AB03 83.0 fits AB02 82.2 (|log| 0.010) and AB09 84.1 (0.013); AB07 77.0 fits AB06 79.1 (0.027) and AB01 78.9 (0.024). Both are clearly not their own mass (113.5, 62.3). So the established count is 'not own mass' in 9 subjects, 'another subject's exact table mass' in 7, and 'previous subject' in 6. AB05's non-level trials (about 113-120 kg) fit its previous subject AB03.
